claims.claim_text: William Disanza was serving in the U.S. Army immediately before being recruited into the OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Disanza describes entering the Army after the Merchant Marine, training with crash boats, and joining OSS during Maryland training; his obituary explicitly says he was recruited from the Army.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence indexed/Army identity, with independently concordant Museum interview and obituary.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit Army-to-OSS transition; the source does not name a specific Army unit or transition date.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment is not the last civilian employer. The Army institution is normalized to an existing organization record.

claims.claim_text: Before Army and OSS service, William Disanza worked as a merchant seaman; the reviewed account does not name a shipping employer.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Disanza says he entered the U.S. Merchant Marine in 1940, worked shipboard deck/watch duties, then left to join the Army.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Direct named first-person interview tied to the indexed person by protected Army identifier and OSS context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Merchant Marine work explicitly precedes Army service and OSS recruitment; no final civilian employer can be identified from the ship names.
claims.match_notes: A vessel name is not proof of the employing shipping company; retain this as occupation only.
